options.B: Inside a separate appendix at the back of the book
options.C: Inside the body paragraphs near the borrowed information
options.D: Only on the title page beneath the student name

explanation: You've got this! In-text citations sit right inside your paragraphs to point readers to your sources instantly.

question: How do learning management systems particularly benefit nurses who work rotating shift duties?

options.A: By allowing them to complete mandatory training modules at their own convenience
options.B: By exempting them from all practical hospital exams and clinical hours
options.C: By providing free mobile phones for personal communication use
options.D: By automatically writing their patient care notes during night shifts

explanation: Because these platforms are available online around the clock, nurses can fit their continuing education around irregular shift schedules. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T5#GNS113_U3_T5_h5)

question: Which germs are the most common causes of Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID)?

options.A: Candida albicans and Trichomonas vaginalis
options.B: Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus
options.C: Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae
options.D: Human papillomavirus and Herpes simplex virus

explanation: PID usually happens when sexually transmitted bacteria travel upward from the vagina and cervix into the uterus and fallopian tubes. Always good to remember for clinicals!

question: What is a main nursing duty right when a disaster hits and patients start coming in?

options.A: Funding international relief groups
options.B: Sorting and triaging injured patients
options.C: Rewriting national health emergency policies
options.D: Designing permanent building rules

explanation: During an emergency, checking and sorting patients by how badly they need help is a core nursing job. You've got a bright future in healthcare!

question: Roughly what percentage of a healthy adult's body weight is water?

options.A: 60 percent
options.B: 5 percent
options.C: 90 percent
options.D: 20 percent

explanation: Water makes up about 60% of an adult body! It is the fluid highway where almost all cellular activities happen.

question: What do the letters in the SBAR communication tool stand for?

options.A: Symptoms, Body, Analysis, Response
options.B: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.C: Safety, Behavior, Action, Review
options.D: Staff, Bedside, Assessment, Report

explanation: SBAR provides a standardized, concise framework for sharing critical patient updates among health professionals. [learn more](GST321_U7_T1#GST321_U7_T1_h7)

question: When should discharge planning ideally start for a patient in subacute care?

options.A: After physical therapy finishes
options.B: Forty-eight hours before leaving
options.C: When the family requests it
options.D: On the day of admission

explanation: Spot on! Starting on day one ensures home changes, equipment, and family training are sorted out without last-minute rush.

question: Why are local disaster teams so important when an emergency strikes?

options.A: They handle all federal immigration policies during a crisis
options.B: They are the first responders on the ground before national agencies arrive
options.C: They have unlimited financial resources to rebuild destroyed communities
options.D: They replace the need for hospital-based nursing care entirely

explanation: Spot on! Local teams are already right there where crises happen, making them the immediate first line of defense while distant federal help gets moving.

question: How does a harsh, fault-finding work culture affect clinical safety?

options.A: It helps supervisors finish their administrative duties much faster
options.B: It forces junior nurses to study their textbooks more frequently
options.C: It encourages staff to report every single minor incident immediately
options.D: It makes nurses hide mistakes out of fear, preventing learning and improvement

explanation: When the environment is too scary, people hide their errors instead of talking about them. True learning happens in safe, open spaces!

question: What is the main goal of Targeted Temperature Management (TTM) after cardiac arrest?

options.A: To melt any blood clots inside the coronary arteries
options.B: To stimulate the heart to beat faster on its own
options.C: To protect the brain from injury by controlling body temperature
options.D: To help the kidneys filter out emergency medications

explanation: Cooling the body helps reduce brain swelling and metabolic demand after oxygen deprivation. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T4#GNS315_U4_T4_h7)

question: A patient comes to the clinic with severe lower belly pain and irregular bleeding. What is the best first nursing action?

options.A: Take a detailed menstrual history, including her last period date
options.B: Prepare her for immediate surgery
options.C: Tell the patient menopause has started
options.D: Advise her to stop all physical activity

explanation: Brilliant! Always start with a thorough history. Knowing her menstrual pattern helps the team figure out what might be going wrong.

question: Why do researchers use the exact same questions and words for everyone taking a survey?

options.A: It prevents participants from feeling confused by long medical terms
options.B: It guarantees that every participant will finish the survey faster
options.C: It allows the nurse researcher to change the topic mid-interview
options.D: It ensures all answers can be fairly compared across the group

explanation: Using identical wording means any differences in the responses are due to actual differences between people, not because a question was asked differently. Keep pushing forward!

question: When planning a new health program in a village, why is it vital for a nurse to involve local leaders?

options.A: To shift all financial responsibility onto the community members
options.B: To replace the need for professional nursing assessments
options.C: To comply with international travel regulations
options.D: To ensure the program respects local values and gains community acceptance

explanation: Well done! Working with local leaders builds trust and makes sure your health projects fit nicely with the culture and lifestyle of the people.

question: What process did Louis Pasteur invent to keep drinks like milk and wine from spoiling?

options.A: Pasteurization
options.B: Ultraviolet irradiation
options.C: Chemical chlorination
options.D: Fractional distillation

explanation: Pasteurization uses controlled heat to knock out spoilage germs in liquids without ruining how they taste. Think of pasteurized milk!

question: What type of health issue usually spikes during the first few hours of a sudden disaster?

options.A: Delayed seasonal allergy symptoms
options.B: Acute physical trauma and injuries
options.C: Chronic degenerative nerve disorders
options.D: Long-term nutritional deficiencies

explanation: Right after sudden events like storms or earthquakes, the most common sights are physical injuries, cuts, and fractures that need immediate care.

question: What is a point source of water pollution?

options.A: A distinct, identifiable location like a factory pipe
options.B: Windblown dust falling randomly over a lake
options.C: Underground seepage from multiple small homes
options.D: Widespread rainfall runoff from a large farm

explanation: Point sources release pollutants from a single, fixed spot that is easy to spot and regulate. [learn more](GST114_U3_T3#GST114_U3_T3_h3)

question: Why is clinical relevance so important when reviewing a research paper?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any statistical calculations in the paper
options.B: It proves whether the authors paid their publishing fees on time
options.C: A study can be methodologically sound yet completely useless for your specific patient group
options.D: It guarantees that the journal has a high academic impact factor

explanation: Even if a study is well-designed, we must check if its findings actually make sense and work safely for the specific patients we care for every day.

question: What is the main reason behind the heavy migration of Nigerian nurses and doctors abroad?

options.A: Search for better pay and working conditions abroad
options.B: Lack of nursing training schools within the country
options.C: Mandatory international service for all nursing graduates
options.D: Complete closure of local hospitals by the government

explanation: You nailed it. Low pay, heavy workloads, and safety concerns push many healthcare professionals to look for greener pastures overseas.

question: Which of these is NOT a major challenge facing healthcare financing in Nigeria?

options.A: Heavy reliance on out-of-pocket payments by ordinary citizens
options.B: Excessive availability of well-managed public funds in primary centers
options.C: Inefficient resource distribution and management weaknesses
options.D: Inadequate budgetary allocations from government tiers

explanation: You got it! Primary health centers definitely do *not* have excess funds; rather, they struggle with severe underfunding and poor management.

question: Why should the person who orders hospital supplies be different from the person who approves the payment?

options.A: To ensure that nurses never have to handle administrative paperwork
options.B: To maintain separation of duties and reduce the risk of fraud
options.C: To allow the finance department to dictate clinical patient care
options.D: To make sure orders take longer to process through the system

explanation: Separating these duties creates a safety net. When two different people handle ordering and paying, it greatly reduces the chance of theft or financial mix-ups.

question: Which of these is an example of using an endoscope for treatment (therapeutic)?

options.A: Measuring the patient's resting blood pressure
options.B: Taking a routine chest X-ray of the lungs
options.C: Drawing blood for a complete blood count
options.D: Removing a polyp from the colon lining

explanation: Great job! When we use a scope to actively fix something—like snipping out a polyp—it's therapeutic. If we're just looking around, it's diagnostic.

question: A nurse manager wants to graph staff numbers across four units: ICU, Emergency, Pediatrics, and Surgery. Which chart fits best?

options.A: A bar chart, because the departments are separate categories
options.B: A scatter plot, because departments change over time
options.C: A pie chart showing only the ICU department
options.D: A histogram, because staff counts are continuous numbers

explanation: Because these hospital units are distinct, separate groups rather than a continuous scale, a bar chart is the right tool.

question: What does 'evidence-based practice' mean for a working nurse?

options.A: Doing whatever the patient demands regardless of safety
options.B: Relying solely on intuition during emergencies
options.C: Using current best research evidence alongside clinical expertise
options.D: Following hospital traditions without questioning them

explanation: Great choice! EBP blends solid research, your clinical judgment, and what matters to the patient to give the best care.

question: Where does most of the money for public healthcare come from?

options.A: Donations from international pharmaceutical manufacturing corporations
options.B: Profits generated exclusively by private for-profit clinics
options.C: Direct out-of-pocket payments made by emergency room patients
options.D: Government revenue and taxation derived from national economic output

explanation: Public healthcare is funded mostly through taxes and government revenue. When the economy generates wealth, public services get their share.

question: Where are brush border enzymes like lactase and maltase found?

options.A: Embedded in the membrane of small intestine cells
options.B: Floating freely inside the cavity of the stomach
options.C: Released by the gallbladder during fat digestion
options.D: Produced by the salivary glands in the mouth

explanation: These enzymes live right on the microvilli of the small intestine lining, ready to finish breaking down your sugars.

question: Which body regulates the professional scope of practice for midwives in Nigeria?

options.A: West African Health Organization
options.B: Nigerian Medical Association
options.C: Federal Ministry of Women Affairs
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria is the statutory body responsible for setting standards and regulating midwifery practice. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T15#GNS225_U3_T15_h2)

question: Which tool does a nurse grab to take a look inside a patient's ear canal and ear drum?

options.A: An ophthalmoscope
options.B: A tongue depressor
options.C: A stethoscope
options.D: An otoscope

explanation: Spot on! An otoscope has a handy built-in light and magnifier so you can easily check the ear canal and tympanic membrane.

question: How does community-based rehabilitation help fight against social stigma?

options.A: By involving local leaders and educating the public about disabilities
options.B: By forcing communities to build expensive private hospitals
options.C: By restricting public gatherings for people with chronic illnesses
options.D: By hiding individuals with disabilities away from public view

explanation: Education clears up misunderstandings. When local communities learn together, they start seeing the person first, not the disability.

question: Why is it smart for community health nurses to work with local market leaders when promoting food hygiene?

options.A: It stops people from selling food altogether
options.B: It guarantees that the local market will receive government funding
options.C: It helps ensure the hygiene messages are accepted and practiced by vendors
options.D: It allows the nurse to avoid visiting the market stalls personally

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Market leaders are respected, so getting them on board makes food vendors much more willing to listen and adopt safe habits.

question: What is one of the main goals of maternal health services in a displacement camp?

options.A: Providing free formula milk to every newborn infant
options.B: Reducing maternal and neonatal mortality through skilled care
options.C: Eliminating the need for any antenatal checkups
options.D: Mandating home deliveries without professional assistance

explanation: Every mother deserves a safe delivery! Providing skilled midwives and emergency obstetric care saves mothers and newborns from avoidable complications in crisis zones.

question: What is an important teaching point for patients who use non-nutritive sweeteners?

options.A: Patients must take extra insulin every time they consume stevia or sucralose.
options.B: Artificial sweeteners will cause immediate low blood sugar if taken without food.
options.C: Products labeled sugar-free can still contain carbohydrates and calories from other ingredients.
options.D: Sugar substitutes raise blood glucose faster than natural cane sugar.

explanation: Sugar-free packaged foods often contain flour and fats that still impact blood glucose and weight. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T012#GNS227_U6_T012_h5)

question: Which type of food hazard includes cleaning chemicals and leftover pesticide sprays?

options.A: Physical hazards
options.B: Biological hazards
options.C: Nutritional hazards
options.D: Chemical hazards

explanation: You guessed it—chemical hazards involve toxic substances like cleaning agents and farm chemicals that accidentally get into our food supply.

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge faced in community health planning in Nigeria?

options.A: Cultural resistance and rumors regarding certain public health programs
options.B: Excessive availability of surplus financial funds in primary health centers
options.C: Poor transportation infrastructure in remote rural or riverine areas
options.D: Inadequate funding and delayed budgetary releases from government

explanation: Primary health centers in Nigeria typically suffer from chronic underfunding rather than having excessive surplus funds. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h8)

question: Which infection is most directly linked to the development of cervical cancer?

options.A: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
options.B: Human papillomavirus
options.C: Chlamydia trachomatis
options.D: Human immunodeficiency virus

explanation: High-risk strains of human papillomavirus (HPV) can hang around in the cells of the cervix for years and eventually cause cell changes that lead to cancer.

question: How does better nutrition quietly boost a patient's overall quality of life?

options.A: By increasing their financial income through savings
options.B: By ensuring they never experience physical pain again
options.C: By giving them the energy to enjoy daily activities and hobbies
options.D: By making them sleep for twelve hours every night

explanation: Exactly! When chronic fatigue fades away, patients can finally get back to enjoying their daily walks, family gatherings, and favorite hobbies.

question: How long must a patient typically fast (NPO) before a barium swallow examination?

options.A: 30 minutes
options.B: No fasting is needed
options.C: 6 to 8 hours
options.D: 24 full hours

explanation: An empty stomach is required so that food residue does not block the view of the mucosal lining or mimic a tumor on the X-ray. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h3)

question: Besides stopping ovulation, how does progestin help prevent pregnancy?

options.A: By creating an electrical charge in the uterus
options.B: By neutralizing the natural acid levels in the vagina
options.C: By increasing the temperature of the vaginal canal
options.D: By making the cervical mucus thick and hostile

explanation: Progestin changes the consistency of cervical secretions into a thick barrier, making it way too hard for sperm to swim through to meet an egg. Neat, right?

question: Why is the community health planning cycle a continuous loop instead of a straight line?

options.A: Nurses must repeat the exact same paperwork every single month
options.B: Evaluation findings feed back into new assessments to improve future care
options.C: Health problems never change once an intervention is finished
options.D: It stops the community from ever joining in on healthcare

explanation: Exactly! Healthcare doesn't stop. What you learn from evaluating a project helps you plan even better care for the next round.

question: What is one major limitation of using robots in patient care units?

options.A: Robots require continuous physical lifting from bedside nurses
options.B: Robots lack clinical intuition and cannot interpret subtle human emotional cues
options.C: Robots completely eliminate the need for electronic health records
options.D: Robots are incapable of moving along hospital corridors

explanation: Spot on! Machines follow strict programming. They can never fully replace the warm, empathetic touch and observant eye of a real nurse.

question: Why must a nurse always give sedatives or pain meds along with a neuromuscular blocker?

options.A: Sedatives are required to make the neuromuscular blocker start working faster
options.B: Pain medication prevents the sudden drop in blood pressure caused by the blocker
options.C: Neuromuscular blockers cause extreme agitation and anxiety if given alone
options.D: These drugs cause complete paralysis without affecting consciousness or pain

explanation: Remember, paralytics only freeze the muscles—they don't put the patient to sleep or stop pain. Always protect your patient by ensuring they are sedated first!

question: A nurse wants to search for articles mentioning either 'pain' or 'discomfort'. Which search word should be used?

options.A: NOT
options.B: AND
options.C: WITH
options.D: OR

explanation: The word OR tells the database to look for either term, helping you catch helpful synonyms and expand your search.

question: Which of these is an example of a man-made disaster?

options.A: A sudden and destructive hurricane
options.B: A severe regional earthquake
options.C: A major factory chemical explosion
options.D: A massive coastal tidal wave

explanation: Spot on! Factory accidents and chemical spills happen because of human activity, making them man-made, unlike natural weather or earth movements.
